correctness.rationale: For center degree d the two red leaves can be chosen in d(d−1) ordered ways and the blue leaf in n−1−d ways, disjoint from both red leaves. Degrees on A,B,C are n−1,a+b−1,a on the nonempty classes, with m=binom(a+b,2)+ac, including the zero-class cases. Independently exhausted (a,h) with 0≤a≤h≤n and (a,b,c)=(a,h−a,n−h). For each order I constructed actual adjacency matrices: a pair u<v is in H iff u<a or v<h, and Q and S use the first and last m pairs in order of increasing v then u, respectively. The first m pairs give exactly the full clique and partial next vertex, including m=0 and complete graphs; the last m are the complement of the first binom(n,2)−m. The exact run covered 1767 triples; none improved on both endpoints through n=19. The complete n=20 output in (a,b,c;m;H,Q,S) order is (6,12,2;165;7308,7860,7344) and (7,11,2;167;6992,7370,7072). Literal ordered four-vertex counts checked all three graphs for each witness and every profile through n=8. The frozen enumeration and recorded log agree; the independent enumeration did not execute the frozen script.
residual_risks: The cutoff is only within H_{a,b,c} and orders 2–20; it does not give a global minimizer at either edge count or a cutoff for all graphs.

evidence: The known construction/count identity reduces the task to finite integer comparisons. A strict limiting gap may give examples at sufficiently large orders but gives neither a lower bound excluding every smaller order nor equality cases for a finite discrete strict-comparison census.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Determining the crossover and enumerating all first-order exceptions still requires exact finite work; neither follows by substituting parameters in a prior theorem.

evidence: Complementation exchanges red and blue and interchanges quasi-clique and quasi-star. The family in the complemented problem is K_c joined to an independent b-set, with a isolates. The two exact complementary witnesses have 25 and 23 edges, respectively.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Deng–Hou's construction covers this same family, even after exchanging edge colors; their asymptotic comparison does not state the complemented exact cutoff and the two finite triples either.
